content.title: Research Guides: Health of United States Presidents: 25th Amendment Titles
content.text: The following books and articles include materials focus on the 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Proposed by Congress and ratified by the states in the aftermath of the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, the 25th Amendment provides the procedures for replacing the president or vice president in the event of death, removal, resignation, or incapacitation. Books Articles Amendment XXV by Call Number: KF5082 .A85 2010 ISBN: 9780737746983 Published/Created: 2010-05-03 History of the Twenty-fifth Amendment--the Twenty-fifth Amendment in Action--Limitations of the Twenty-fifth Amendment--Solutions to potential problems of presidential succession and disability. Resources for further research: p. 194-199. Medical Cover-Ups in the White House by Edward B. MacMahon; Leonard Curry Call Number: E176.1 .M28 1987 ISBN: 0918535018 Published/Created: 1987-08-01 Includes a brief history of the role of White House physician and the illnesses of certain presidents. There are individual chapters on Presidents Garfield, Cleveland, Wilson, Harding, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Eisenhower, Kennedy, Carter, and Reagan. Presidential Leadership, Illness, and Decision Making by Rose McDermott Call Number: JK609 .M124 2008 ISBN: 9780521882729 Published/Created: 2007-12-10 The effects of presidential medical and psychological illnesses on a president’s ability to make decisions are discussed. The illnesses of Woodrow Wilson, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Dwight D. Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy, and Richard Nixon are debated at some length. The effect of the illness of foreign leaders on presidential decisions is also discussed, using the example of President Carter’s response to the illness of the Shah of Iran. Briefly reviewed are the illnesses of presidents from George Washington to George H. W. Bush. Bibliography: p. 293-304. Cerebrum: the Dana forum on brain science by Toole, James F. Call Number: QP376 .C424 Published/Created: Oct. 1, 1998 Toole, James F. When an American president “loses it.” Oct. 1, 1998: 38-46. Dr. Toole, who headed the Working Group on Presidential Disability, discusses the disabilities of Presidents Wilson, Roosevelt, and Eisenhower, and suggests steps to protect the president and the nation should such disabilities occur in future presidents.
